title: Register every class an event can be, or refuse to start

blocks.text: The event bus writes a type id into every message it sends and reads it back to pick the class to decode into. A message whose class has no id fails, and it fails in production, at the first message of that class. So at startup `TypeRegistry.of(Event.class)` registers every class a message can have at run time, by walking the sealed hierarchy under `Event`.
Last month a team added a class to the hierarchy that the registry never saw, and the first message of that class was lost. The registry should never start in a state where that can happen.

Finish `collect(Class<?> type)` in `src/main/java/practice/TypeRegistry.java`. When you're done, `of(root)` registers exactly the classes a value of `root` can have, and it throws `IllegalArgumentException`, naming the class, when the hierarchy lets in classes that no list names. About eight lines in total.
The tests build their own hierarchies, with records, classes and interfaces at more than one level.

cases.says: every record and final class permitted by a sealed interface is registered, and the interface itself is not
the final subclasses of an abstract sealed root are registered, and the abstract root is not
a non-sealed class below a sealed root makes the registry refuse, naming that class
a sealed class that is not abstract is registered itself, as well as its permitted subclasses
a sealed subclass keeps the hierarchy closed: its permitted subclasses are registered and nothing is refused
a non-sealed interface below a sealed root makes the registry refuse, naming that interface

origin.section: non-sealed Reopens One Branch, and Subtypes Nobody Listed Arrive Through Its Case

concepts: A non-sealed subclass or subinterface lets any class extend it, so the set of classes below a sealed root is no longer known.
A sealed subclass keeps the hierarchy closed below it: only its own permitted subclasses can extend it.
A sealed subclass that is not abstract has instances of its own, so covering its permitted subclasses does not cover it.
